title: Arbitrary base change of supplied coherent relative dualizing pairs
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be separated, flat and locally of finite presentation, let $g:S'\to S$ be any scheme morphism, and form $X'=X\times_SS'$ with projection $g_X$ and morphism $f':X'\to S'$ [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $(K,\xi)$ be a supplied coherent relative dualizing pair for $f$ [def-trf-coherent-relative-dualizing-pair]. Put $K'=Lg_X^*K$ [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Under the canonical Tor-independent diagonal base-change identification $L(g_X\times g_X)^*\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\simeq\Delta'_*\mathcal O_{X'}$ and pullback composition, the pullback of $\xi$ is a class $\xi':\Delta'_*\mathcal O_{X'}\to Lp_1'^*K'$. Then $(K',\xi')$ is a coherent relative dualizing pair for $f'$. These pullbacks of objects and classes respect identity and iterated base change. No flatness of $g$ or Noetherianity is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0E2Y, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing; algebraic input dualizing.tex Tag 0E2F, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing.

proof.text: The base-changed morphism $f'$ is flat and separated by the two cited stability lemmas. On a finite-presentation affine chart $R\to A$ for $f$, its pullback over an affine $R\to R'$ is the presentation $R'[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$; the finite-presentation base-change lemma therefore makes $f'$ locally finitely presented. By the supplied-pair definition, $K$ is pseudo-coherent and locally of finite Tor dimension over $S$. Apply scheme relative-perfect base change to obtain these same two properties for $K'$ over $S'$. In particular both complexes have quasi-coherent cohomology by pseudo-coherence.

source.place: Tag 0E2Y, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing; finiteness of the pullback and hypotheses for the affine reduction

proof.text: Write $Y=X\times_SX$, $Y'=X'\times_{S'}X'$ and $h=g_X\times g_X$. Each projection $Y\to X$ is flat by base change, so $Y\to S$ is flat by composition. Apply common-base Tor independence to the $S$-map $\Delta:X\to Y$ between these two flat $S$-schemes. It gives Tor independence of $\Delta$ and $h$. The diagonal is closed, hence quasi-compact and separated. Locally on affine opens of $Y$ and $Y'$, apply Tor-independent derived base change to $\Delta$ with perfect factor $\mathcal O_X$ and quasi-coherent factor $\mathcal O_X$. Closed module pushforward is exact (it preserves homology), so $R\Delta_*\mathcal O_X=\Delta_*\mathcal O_X$, and similarly for $\Delta'$. The resulting canonical map is $d_g:Lh^*\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta'_*\mathcal O_{X'}$. The affine maps glue since each is the restriction of the canonical base-change mate; on an affine chart they are the tensor augmentation onto the diagonal quotient.

source.place: Tag 0E2Y, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing; the Tor-independent diagonal square and its canonical identification

proof.text: Derived pullback composition identifies $Lh^*Lp_1^*K$ with $Lp_1'^*Lg_X^*K=Lp_1'^*K'$, since $p_1h=g_Xp'_1$. Define $\xi'$ to be $d_g^{-1}$ followed by $Lh^*\xi$ and this target comparison. Thus the object and class in the question are defined globally, without making a choice of local dualizing generators.

source.place: Tag 0E2Y, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing; definition of the derived base-changed class

proof.text: Choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset f^{-1}V$ and $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subset g^{-1}V$, using finite-presentation charts for $f$. Let $B=A\otimes_R A$ and $U'=U\times_VV'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$. The affine derived equivalence realizes $K|_U$ by $M\in D(A)$. The affine pseudo-coherence and relative Tor-amplitude criteria give pseudo-coherence over $A$ and one finite $R$-Tor interval for $M$. Applied to $K'|_{U'}$, they give the analogous properties of $M'$. The affine K-flat pullback comparison identifies $M'$ with $M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$ and identifies $Lp_1^*K|_{U\times_VU}$ with $\widetilde{M_1}$, $M_1=M\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B$. To check boundedness below of $M_1$, apply relative-perfect base change to $f$ along itself: $Lp_1^*K$ is relatively perfect over the second copy of $X$. On $U\times_VU$, the affine Tor criterion over that copy of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ gives a finite interval; testing its tensor on $A[0]$ bounds the cohomology of $M_1$. The identical argument with $f'$ bounds $M'_1$.

source.place: Tag 0E2Y, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing; affine-local reduction and all finiteness hypotheses for internal Hom

proof.text: Apply quotient pseudo-coherence to $R\to B\twoheadrightarrow A$, with quotient multiplication, and $A[0]$, which is free of rank one over $A$. Both algebras are flat and finitely presented over $R$: geometrically their maps are $U\times_VU\to V$ and $U\to V$, using flat base change and composition; their polynomial presentations give finite presentation. Thus $A[0]$ is pseudo-coherent over $B$. The same argument gives pseudo-coherence of $A'[0]$ over $B'$. On $U\times_VU$, ordinary diagonal pushforward of $\mathcal O_U$ is $\widetilde A$: on standard opens this is precisely the localized quotient module. The affine algebra-class evaluation comparison now applies to $(B,A,M_1)$ and $(B',A',M'_1)$, since Step 4 checked boundedness below. It identifies each sheaf multiplication map with the associated sheaf of the corresponding algebraic transpose $m_\gamma$, including the actual classes. The K-flat pullback comparison and Step 3 identify the second class with the derived scalar extension $\gamma'$ of the first.

source.place: Tag 0E2Y, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing; affine diagonal algebra, internal Hom and the actual class maps

proof.text: The original multiplication map is an isomorphism by the supplied-pair hypothesis. Steps 4--5 and the affine equivalence therefore give $m_\gamma:A[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A[0],M_1)$. In degree zero it sends $a$ to $a\gamma$ (transpose of multiplication), so $\gamma$ is a generator. Apply the algebraic diagonal-generator base-change lemma. It gives the diagonal Hom object $A'[0]$ and says that $\gamma'$ generates its degree-zero Hom module, which is free of rank one over $A'$. The map $m_{\gamma'}$ induces $a'\mapsto a'\gamma'$ in degree zero, an isomorphism: under any rank-one identification the generator is a unit $u$ and this map is multiplication by $u$. In every other degree both cohomologies vanish. Consequently $m_{\gamma'}$ is an isomorphism, and the class evaluation comparison makes the required sheaf multiplication map an isomorphism on $U'\times_{V'}U'$.

source.place: Tag 0E2Y, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing; algebraic base change, including its generator clause

proof.text: The opens $U'\times_{V'}U'$ used above cover a neighbourhood of the diagonal in $Y'$. On its open complement $\Delta'_*\mathcal O_{X'}$ is zero; restriction of derived internal Hom is internal Hom of the restrictions, hence the other side is zero as well. On the neighbourhoods, restriction of internal Hom and class evaluation identifies the tested map with the restriction of the global multiplication map. It is therefore an isomorphism everywhere: its cone has all cohomology sheaves zero on an open cover and thus globally zero. Together with Step 1 this is exactly the supplied-pair predicate for $(K',\xi')$.

source.place: Tag 0E2Y, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing; passage from the affine test to the global pair

proof.text: For successive base changes $S''\xrightarrow{k}S'\xrightarrow{g}S$, pullback composition identifies $Lh_k^*Lh_g^*\xi$ with $L(h_gh_k)^*\xi$. The canonical diagonal identifications satisfy $d_{gk}=d_k\circ Lh_k^*(d_g)$ under that composition comparison: this is horizontal pasting of the two canonical derived base-change squares for the closed diagonal, with its pullback composition identifications. Its affine normalization also sends $(a\otimes r')\otimes r''$ to $a\otimes k(r')r''$ on both routes. The target comparisons commute by associativity of derived pullback composition. Substituting these two equalities in Step 3 proves equality of the two resulting classes and the usual composition comparison for the objects. For an identity base change the diagonal augmentation and target comparison are identities under the canonical unit identifications. Thus identity and iterated base change respect both objects and classes.
